title: Instance blueprint
description: An instance blueprint (#117, #823): what an instance is loaded from besides its region, regions/<id>.md or the region pieces in regions/<id>/. One file per blueprint, named after its id. Saved worlds and quests name an instance by its id, so an id is never reused or changed once shipped.

id.description: Stable, never reused: lowercase words joined by underscores, the name of its region too.

codex.description: Its codex entry (#959): what the player reads on its codex page.

entry.description: A short text about it and where its name comes from.

gloss.description: What its name means, hand-written (#959), e.g. "the soft clearing".

rules.description: The id of its rule set (data/rule_sets/, #941): the rules (features) its instances have, unless add_rules or drop_rules change them. A rule is on in an instance only when its blueprint has it (#30, #823). What its region holds brings the features that run it, which are never named here: exits, triggers, region pieces to enter, wild monsters and their hiding, people, and treasure chests, which a chest_table brings too (#879). They step in the order the blueprints slice's FeatureFactories gives them, which also lists the ids there are.

add_rules.description: The ids of rules its rule set lacks that its instances have too, each once (#941).

drop_rules.description: The ids of rules in its rule set that its instances don't have, each once (#941). At least one rule must be left.

turned.description: Whether the seed turns its region pieces (#57, #127); false keeps the layout they're drawn in. Every instance in the web of exits keeps it, so an exit always leads out the same way (#120). A region file is never turned.

loot_table.description: Its instance loot table (the loot slice's data/loot_tables/): what a blank and the loot on its ground give (#90, #203).

chest_table.description: Its chest loot table (the loot slice's data/loot_tables/): its treasure chests roll on it (#124, #694). A blueprint with one needs a loot_table too, for the loot on its ground.

wild_species.description: Which species live in it, and how likely each is, for the wild monster spots its region doesn't name (#133): species id to weight, rolled in the order written.

variants.description: Its variants (#529, #541): the first entry whose world flag is set chooses its region, so a later story beat listed first overrides an earlier one. The rest of the blueprint stays.

flag.description: The world flag that chooses it.

region.description: The region it's loaded with instead, a region file or a folder of region pieces in regions/; "" for the blueprint's own. A region of its own is named, its name its id in words (#909).

codex.description: The codex entry (#959) of the region it loads, which a variant with a region of its own has.

entry.description: A short text about it and where its name comes from.
